belief: Everyone else is better than me.
origins: Constant comparison in school, work, and social settings convinces some that they are at the bottom. This belief shrinks risk-taking, friendships, and joy.
teaches: Paul writes, “Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.” “Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment.” And God “has composed the body… so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another” (1 Corinthians 12:24–25). Different gifts are not better or worse; they are needed. You have your place and your part.
self_statements: They are smarter, kinder, and more capable.
errors: Believing I am either best or worst.
Predicting that I will always be inferior.
Feeling small and concluding that I am.
questions: Who exactly am I comparing myself to?
What do I not see about their struggles?
What gifts do I have that others lack?
What does Scripture say about each member of the body?
truth: Everyone has different gifts, and mine are needed. I can test my own work, thank God for others’ strengths, and be at peace with my own.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I do not need to compare.
log: Each week, note one contribution you made.
prayer: Lord, I compare myself and feel small. Show me my gifts, free me from comparison, and let me enjoy my part in Your body. Amen.
